paper.title_en: Quasi-long-range order in the quantum XY model on Sierpiński gaskets
paper.abstract_en: Fractal geometry has recently been shown to enhance the amplitude of the superconducting order parameter, but the fate of the superconducting phase on such lattices is far less clear. Classical XY models on finitely ramified fractals have no finite-temperature transition, as the energy of a vortex stays bounded as the system grows. However, that statement concerns an infinite gasket and thermal vortices, while real fractal structures are finite by construction. It also leaves open what happens at $T = 0$, where the phase competes not with temperature but with its own quantum fluctuations. In this work we address whether superconducting phase coherence survives at $T=0$. To that end, we study the spin-$1/2$ XY ferromagnet, the phase sector of a Josephson network with at most one Cooper pair per island, thus capturing the maximum effect of quantum phase fluctuations, on both triangular and honeycomb Sierpiński gaskets. By using vision-transformer neural quantum states optimized by variational Monte Carlo, we reach generations up to $G = 5$, that is $366$ sites for the triangular gasket and $609$ for the honeycomb one, well beyond the reach of exact diagonalization. We find that the transverse two-point correlator decays algebraically, $C_{xy}(r) \sim r^{-η}$ with $η\simeq 0.12\!-\!0.32$, independent of distance measured along the graph, along the fractal boundary, or in the embedding plane. Quantum phase fluctuations thus leave quasi-long-range order intact in the ground state. We further discuss the implication of these results for the superconducting response of a finite gasket at low but nonzero temperature.
